title: Water evaporates readily at the boil and much more slowly near freezing
summary: Water evaporates readily at its boiling point and much more slowly near freezing, because evaporation still needs heat.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says water easily evaporates at its boiling point but evaporates much more slowly at its freezing point, because of the heat energy required. The page prints Fahrenheit and Celsius labels for those two points. Those scale numbers already live on the linked NIST card, including the word about on the Celsius boil, so they are not copied here. The claim on this card is the contrast in speed, not a new measurement of either point.

sources.title: Evaporation and the Water Cycle
sources.author: U.S. Geological Survey
sources.note: U.S. Geological Survey page, U.S. government work, public domain. Supports faster evaporation at the boiling point than at the freezing point. Numerals are not repeated. Byline date 8 June 2019.
